title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: HubSpot connector in the Researcher agent
summary: The licensing, roadmap facts and Researcher's read-only behaviour are supported. The staged-rollout route combines a connector details-pane route with an Add staging action documented in the connections list; that sequence could leave an administrator unable to find the next step.

claims.claim: The HubSpot connector lets Researcher use third-party HubSpot information to enrich generated answers.
claims.quote: The HubSpot connector allows users using the Researcher agent to be able to leverage 3rd party information from HubSpot to enrich generated responses with relevant information.

claims.claim: Current documentation does not state HubSpot's unconditional default arrival state.

claims.claim: Federated connectors require Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licensing or Microsoft 365 E7 for tenants and users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Connector grounding incurs no extra charges for organisations with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for federated connector publisher-type access settings.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors Agent and plugin access API PowerShell. Read manage-federated-connectors, overview and graph/connecting-external-content-connectors-api-overview; found UI controls and ingestion APIs, not an operation setting federated publisher access.

claims.claim: Publisher types are controlled in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access > publisher type.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access. Clear the publisher types you want to block:

claims.claim: Agent and plugin access governs existing and future federated connectors by publisher type across the organisation.
claims.quote: Turn off all connectors of a publisher type (Microsoft, your organization, or external publishers) in a single step. Apply that choice automatically to future connectors of that type.

claims.claim: Clearing a publisher type sets existing connectors of that type to staged rollout No users.
claims.quote: When you clear an option, existing connectors of that type remain visible to admins in Copilot connectors > Your connections, but their staged rollout is set to No users.

claims.claim: The management page names Global Administrator or Search Administrator as the role needed to manage federated connectors.
claims.quote: To manage federated connectors, you need one of the following administrator roles: Global Administrator; Search Administrator.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for the federated connector User access ceiling.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors User access Graph API. Read manage-federated-connectors and graph/connecting-external-content-connectors-api-overview; returned connector overviews and ingestion APIs, not an operation setting this user population.

claims.claim: User access is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: User access in Agents > Settings applies to all agents and plugins, including federated connectors delivered as Microsoft 365 app packages.

claims.claim: User access is a tenant-wide ceiling on who can use agents, plugins and federated connectors.
claims.quote: User access doesn't turn connectors on or off; it sets the maximum population. A connector whose details pane shows Everyone is still unavailable to users excluded by User access.

claims.claim: User access offers All users by default, Specific users or groups, and No users.
claims.quote: All users (default) | Connector-level staging decides who gets each connector. Specific users or groups | Only these users can use any connector. No users | No user can use connectors, regardless of connector-level settings.

claims.claim: Connector staging can narrow but cannot widen the User access population.
claims.quote: Only these users can use any connector. Connector staging can narrow but not widen this population.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented to enable or disable this federated connector.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors staged rollout enable API. Read overview, manage-federated-connectors, custom-connector management excerpts and graph/connecting-external-content-connectors-api-overview; found UI enable/disable, not a federated connector enable/disable API.

claims.claim: The HubSpot enable/disable control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot connectors > Your connections > connector > Enable/disable data source.
claims.quote: Admins can manage federated Copilot connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center by choosing Copilot connectors > Your connections. Screenshot of the HubSpot connector in the admin center with Staged rollout and Enable/disable data source highlighted.

claims.claim: An individual federated connector can be enabled or disabled at tenant level.
claims.quote: Enable or disable connectors at the tenant level.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for federated connector staged rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors staged rollout enable API. Read overview, manage-federated-connectors, staged-rollout and graph/connecting-external-content-connectors-api-overview; found staged-rollout UI and ingestion APIs, not an operation setting federated staging.

claims.claim: Add staging is reached by opening a connector, then Staged rollout, then Add staging.
claims.quote: Searched: HubSpot Add staging Staged rollout connector. Read overview, staged-rollout and custom-connector management excerpts. Overview places Add staging in the list's Staged rollout column; no passage gives Add staging after opening a connector's Staged rollout pane.
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].ui.path and its rendered copy with 'Copilot connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout > Add staging'. The cited overview says to choose Add staging in the Staged rollout column; retain the note identifying the connector's users or groups. https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/federated-connectors-overview

claims.claim: Staged rollout limits a connector to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups.
claims.quote: Limit a connector to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups by choosing Add staging in the Staged rollout column.

claims.claim: Federated connector blocking is managed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools.
claims.quote: Tools block / unblock | Agents > Tools | Tool-level and connector-level blocking.

claims.claim: Tools block / unblock supports both tool-level and connector-level blocking of federated connectors.
claims.quote: Tools block / unblock | Agents > Tools | Tool-level and connector-level blocking.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use MCP to fetch data and responses dynamically in real time.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time. Responses are fetched dynamically from the data source via MCP.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated access follows the user's identity and source-system permissions.
claims.quote: The authenticated user's identity and permissions in the source system govern tool access. Users can only access information they're authorized to view and change data they're authorized to modify.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Users discover an enabled federated source in Researcher's Sources menu.
claims.quote: Users can discover the data source in the Sources menu in the Researcher agent, in deep research mode in Microsoft 365 Copilot chat, and in Copilot Chat where available.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users authenticate to federated sources with their own credentials when prompted.
claims.quote: Users authenticate by using their own credentials when prompted to connect to the data sources.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Earlier preview documentation described federated connectors as enabled by default for a tenant.
claims.quote: Federated Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors overview (early access preview) ... Federated connectors are enabled by default for a tenant.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Earlier preview documentation gave Microsoft-published connectors a seven-calendar-day admin-only review window before user availability.
claims.quote: When a Microsoft-published federated connector first appears in the admin center, it's available only to admins for seven calendar days before it's available to users.

claims.claim: Earlier preview documentation listed HubSpot under Microsoft-published federated connectors.
claims.quote: Microsoft-published federated connectors ... Microsoft provides a set of federated connectors by default. Currently, federated connectors are available for the following data sources: 1. Canva 2. HubSpot

claims.claim: Current documentation makes Microsoft-built connectors available by default when the Microsoft publisher option is selected and User access includes the user.
claims.quote: Microsoft-built federated connectors are available by default when you select Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft in Agent and plugin access and include the user in User access.

claims.claim: External-publisher connectors are available only when their publisher option is selected or an admin enables the individual connector.
claims.quote: Connectors from external publishers are available only when you select Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers, or when an admin turns on the individual connector.

claims.claim: The current gallery does not name HubSpot's publisher type.
claims.quote: Searched: HubSpot federated connector default publisher settings. Read current overview gallery and management page; CRM lists HubSpot without a publisher column. Search also returned an explicitly earlier-preview Microsoft-published list, not a current HubSpot classification.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents OAuth 2.0 for federated connector access and authentication.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents encrypted communication for federated connector access and authentication.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.claim: An MCP server restricting incoming source IP addresses must allow Microsoft 365 Copilot's static egress addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools belong to the connector and are not enabled separately.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.claim: The admin connector-tool view is labelled Coming soon and is not available for every connector.
claims.quote: View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon) ... Viewing tools in the admin center isn't available for all connectors.

claims.claim: User visibility requires an allowed publisher type or individual admin enablement.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: The connector's publisher type is allowed in Agent and plugin access, or an admin turned on the connector individually.

claims.claim: User visibility requires the connector to be enabled.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The connector is enabled.

claims.claim: User visibility requires inclusion in User access.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user is included in User access.

claims.claim: User visibility requires inclusion in connector staged rollout.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user is included in the connector's staged rollout.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio licences do not support federated Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go does not support federated Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: The prerequisites list a Copilot add-on licence for every user querying a federated source.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license for every user who queries the federated source. For an eligibility matrix, see Licensing.

claims.claim: The cited Microsoft connector documentation does not state HubSpot subscription costs.
claims.quote: Searched: HubSpot federated settings subscription cost. Read connector overview and prerequisites; neither prices HubSpot subscriptions. Search returned unrelated subscription pricing and a HubSpot SSO prerequisite, not federated-connector source subscription prices.

claims.claim: Individual connector settings take precedence over bulk Agent and plugin access, while User access always applies.
claims.quote: A setting you make on an individual connector takes precedence over the bulk Agent and plugin access setting. User access always applies.

claims.claim: Users can turn off a data source in Researcher.
claims.quote: Users can disable the data source at any time by turning off the source in Researcher or by managing the source in Copilot Chat settings.

claims.claim: Connector publishers can add or change tools over time.
claims.quote: The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.claim: The overview names Purview auditing without giving its navigation path.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview and audit within the fetched federated-connectors-overview. Read its connector definition and security/compliance sections; it says admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview but contains no auditing navigation steps.

claims.claim: The prerequisites page requires an AI administrator to configure and deploy Copilot connectors.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
